newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes mostly lower, remains rangebound.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes mostly lower, remains rangebound.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed mostly lower after a day in which the market struggled to establish a clear trend.

Dealers noted prices fell early with stops triggered as the market broke below key support at $3.65 a bushel on September. Scale-down commercial buying halted the fall and buying linked to a sharp advance in nearby soybean prices helped to move the market into positive territory.
Buying interest, however, appeared to evaporate late, prompting a slide down to a mostly lower finish. September ended off 1-3/4 cents at $3.64-1/2 a bushel.
Dealers said the market remained within its recent trading range of around $3.60 to $3.85 on the September contract.

September had risen to a two-month high of $3.83 earlier in the week but news that the Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service had forecast the state's wheat crop at a record 492 million bushels helped to reverse the market's trend.
Other months ended 2-3/4 cents lower to three cents higher.
Volume on wheat was estimated at 31.5 million bushels compared with 45.4 million on Thursday.
